question.text: An organic compound (P) having molecular mass 180 is acylated with <math><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></math> to get a new compound with molecular mass 348. The number of amino groups present per molecule of compound (P) is

solution.text:
R−NH2M+CH3COCl→RNHCOCH3M+42+HCl
If the increase in molecular mass is 42, the reactant has one NH2 group.
Actual increase in molecular mass =348-180=168
Number of NH2 groups =16842=4
